question: Why does a clarinet jump a twelfth, not an octave, when the player opens its register key?
answer: Because its bore is a cylinder closed at the reed end, and such a pipe resonates mainly at odd multiples of its lowest frequency: 1, 3, 5 times. The next resonance up is three times the fundamental, an octave plus a fifth. The same physics leaves its low notes hollow, weak in the even harmonics.
move: The shape of the container picks which notes it can hold.
ask: Which of my limits comes from the shape of what I am working in, not from me?
source: Fletcher & Rossing, Physics of Musical Instruments, 1998
reference: Fletcher and Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd edition, Springer, 1998
